Subject: Cost gating hypotheses for Avalon pilot - MAP inputs

Alex / Procurement team —

Following our kickoff call, attaching a compact list of cost gating hypotheses we plan to validate as part of the MAP. To make the evaluation practical on our side please send the usage profile mentioned on the call (typical user flows, expected QPS, percent of requests with >1024 tokens, peak concurrency windows).

In particular, items we'd like to lock into the MAP and finance checks:
- Baseline tokens/request (avg and 95th) per flow
- Expected cacheable prefix rate (templates / identical starts)
- Burst profile: sustained vs brief spikes (seconds, minutes)
- SLA goals (p50/p95 latency targets) that matter for the application

We're preparing a small cost workbook (attached) that maps tokens/$ for hosted vs dedicated, and models caching + batching impacts. If you can share the usage workbook and any procurement timing constraints we will:
1) run a quick sensitivity analysis and populate the MAP cost page
2) propose a gating threshold (tokens/$) for pilot acceptance and a recommended canary capacity plan

Attachments: redwood_map_cost_workbook.xlsx (blank workbook, assumptions tab)

Goal: have a validated cost section in the MAP by next Friday so procurement has a quantified run-rate for the POC.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher

sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Cost gating hypotheses for Avalon pilot - MAP inputs

Thanks Sean — attaching the usage profile (see sheet names for weekly vs peak). A few clarifications up front:
- Primary flow (clinical triage) averages ~380 tokens/request, 95th ~1,150 tokens.
- Approximately 28% of requests start from a shared template (typical triage prompts) — we flagged that as cacheable at the prefix level.
- Baseline QPS: 6 sustained across business hours, peak burst up to ~90 QPS for 45s per spike (roughly once/day).
- Peak concurrency target during spikes: we expect up to 220 concurrent sessions in a worst-case day.
- Data residency: pilot must keep PHI within us-east-1, and audit logs retained for 1 year.

We don't have an exact procurement cadence yet but are aiming to decide vendor and capacity by mid July.

Attachment: avalon_usage_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Alex Morales
VP Product, Avalon Health
alex.morales@avalonhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morales <alex.morales@avalonhealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost gating hypotheses for Avalon pilot - MAP inputs

Alex — great detail, thanks. Replied inline with the assumptions we'll use to populate the MAP cost page and a short sensitivity sketch. Quoting your key lines below for clarity.

> Primary flow (clinical triage) averages ~380 tokens/request, 95th ~1,150 tokens.
> ~28% of requests start from a shared template (cacheable at prefix level).
> Baseline QPS: 6 sustained, peak burst up to ~90 QPS for 45s, expected peak concurrency 220.

Assumptions we'll model (and why):
- Hosted baseline tokens/$ (gpt-style open quant) = 8.5K tokens per $1 (current verified host pricing for the candidate model)
- Dedicated baseline (reserved GPU) effective tokens/$ = 26K tokens per $1 after utilization and amortized infra (subject to final instance sizing)
- Cache hit rate: conservative 30%, optimistic 55% depending on how many prompts are exact-prefix matches; we'll model both. Cached hits avoid full forward pass for the cached prefix (saves ~30-55% compute depending on prefix length).
- Batching window: to meet p95 latency < 450ms we expect to use a small batching window (20-50ms) for most requests; that yields about 1.4–2.2x throughput improvement for typical batchable flows. We'll include a 1.6x uplift in mid-case calculations.

Quick sensitivity sketch (mid-case numbers):
- Baseline avg tokens/session: 380 tokens * 1 request = 380 tokens -> with 30% cache hit reduces net token compute to ~266 tokens
- Tokens/$ hosted mid-case: 8.5K tokens/$ -> cost per request (compute) ~0.0313 USD (380/8500) -> with caching ~0.0198 USD
- Tokens/$ dedicated mid-case: 26K tokens/$ -> cost per request ~0.0146 USD -> with caching ~0.0096 USD

Implications for MAP gates:
- Suggest pilot acceptance if expected monthly token spend delta (hosted vs dedicated) < 20% and eviction/default burst capacity plan included. For Avalon numbers, dedicated looks materially cheaper at scale but sensitivity to cache hit rate is significant — i.e., if caching is <20% the delta shrinks.

Questions to close in the MAP:
1) Can you confirm typical prompt prefix lengths (avg # tokens in the template portion) so we can refine cache savings?
2) Are you willing to accept a short (50–100ms) p95 latency bump during 90 QPS spikes if it materially reduces unit cost on dedicated?
3) Any firm procurement cutoffs (contract sign-by) beyond mid July?

I've populated the attached redwood_map_cost_workbook.xlsx with mid/low/high scenarios and a simple monthly run-rate tab — see sheet 'MAP inputs'. We can iterate quickly once you confirm prefix length and procurement timing.

Attachment: redwood_map_cost_workbook.xlsx (assumptions + scenarios)

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost gating hypotheses for Avalon pilot - MAP inputs

Karthik — this is exactly the kind of decomposition we needed, thank you. Quick answers:
- Average template prefix for triage flows ~40 tokens (most of the clinical vignette is variable follow-up).
- We're okay with a short p95 latency bump (50–100ms) during the 45s daily spikes for the pilot, provided it's documented in the MAP and remediation (burst autoscale) is included.
- Procurement: target decision week starting 2025-07-14; MSA redline turnaround ideally within 5 business days of vendor selection.

Next steps I'll take on our side: confirm the internal approvers and share a single-sheet SOW (we aim to include data residency clause and 1-year logs retention).

If you can update the MAP cost page with: (a) dedicated vs hosted mid-case numbers, (b) sensitivity rows for cache hit 20/35/55% and (c) recommended pilot acceptance gate (tokens/month threshold + required burst margin) that would be great — aim to circulate updated MAP by EOD Friday (2025-07-04).

Thanks —
Alex Morales
VP Product, Avalon Health
